uncited: The Two-Stage Optimization Pipeline is a post-processing refinement method for 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) that decouples geometric alignment from material/lighting optimization to improve reconstruction quality and enable relighting.

It addresses the limitations of coarse geometry from initial regressors and accumulated pose errors by first correcting camera poses and refining geometry, then locking geometry to optimize material and lighting parameters using pre-computed visibility.

It differs from standard 3DGS by introducing explicit normal vectors and a visibility pre-computation step, and from pose-free methods like [CF3DGS](1036-ray-marching-on-3d-gaussians.md) by using a dedicated pose correction stage.
**Inputs:** A set of registered images, initial camera poses (with seed image pose fixed), and an initial 3D Gaussian point cloud (optionally with normals).
**Outputs:** Optimized camera poses, refined 3D Gaussian primitives (positions, covariances, opacities, colors/coefficients), and optimized material/lighting parameters.
**Geometry Optimization:** Optimize a vanilla 3D Gaussian point cloud augmented with normal vectors $\mathbf{n}$.

*   **When Not to Use:** When real-time performance is critical and two-stage optimization is too slow.
